# Policy fixtures

Each directory holds a `policy.json` in the labfw **file-source bundle format**
(PLAN §4.1): ARM documents exactly as `GET` returns them.

```json
{"policies": [...], "ruleCollectionGroups": {"<policyId>": [...]}, "ipGroups": [...], "serviceTags": {...}}
```

All resource IDs use subscription `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`,
resource group `rg-lab`, location `swedencentral`. Every fixture parses
without warnings (`go test ./internal/policy`). Real exports come from
`scripts/export-policy.sh <policyId> out.json`.

The fixture JSON was generated by a script and is meant to be edited by hand
from now on. Keep `acceptance/policy-a18.json` identical to
`acceptance/policy.json` except for the `allow-a3` collection.

| Fixture | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `basic` | One Standard policy, three RCGs (DNAT 100, network 200, app 300) with typical rules: DNAT `20.0.0.1:2222 → 10.1.0.4:22`, Azure DNS, NTP, spoke-to-spoke `Any`, app rules with `*.ubuntu.com` / `github.com`. |
| `inheritance` | `base-policy` (RCG `base-rcg` priority **500**) and `child-policy` (`basePolicy` → base; RCGs priority 100/200). Base `deny-echo-from-base` and child `allow-echo-in-child` match the same flow (`10.1.0.10 → 198.51.100.11:8080/tcp`): expected **deny** because base rules come first (S2, A6). Base also has an `fqdnTags: [WindowsUpdate]` app rule. |
| `ipgroups` | Three IP groups (CIDR, single IP and range `10.3.0.10-10.3.0.20`), used as NAT `sourceIpGroups`, network `sourceIpGroups`/`destinationIpGroups`, mixed `sourceAddresses` + `sourceIpGroups`, app `sourceIpGroups`; port list with range `9000-9010` (S5, S6, A20). |
| `servicetags` | A small fake service-tags response (`Storage`, regional `Storage.SwedenCentral` and `Storage.WestEurope`, `AzureKeyVault`, `AzureMonitor`, with some IPv6 prefixes) and network rules using them. `unknown-tag` references `NoSuchServiceTag` → that rule is skipped with a diagnostic (S5). |
| `unsupported` | Premium policy using everything in §5.6 on **allow** rules only, so it compiles with warnings: `threatIntelMode: Deny` (+ whitelist), `intrusionDetection` (mode Deny), `explicitProxy`, `sql`, `insights`, `snat.autoLearnPrivateRanges: Enabled` and `privateRanges: ["IANAPrivateRanges"]`, an IPv6 DNS server, IPv6 entries in a network rule (`ipv6-mixed` keeps its IPv4 part, `ipv6-only` matches nothing), wildcard network FQDN (S14a), `webCategories`, `Mssql`, `httpHeadersToInsert`, invalid FQDN pattern `www.*.test` (S11), `targetUrls` with a path on Https without `terminateTLS` (S27), unknown `fqdnTags`. |
| `unsupported-deny` | A **deny** rule with `webCategories`: hard compile error unless `unsupported.allowSkippingDenyRules: true` (PLAN §2 principle 4, §5.6). |
| `acceptance` | The policy for the acceptance matrix (PLAN §9.4), see below. |

## Acceptance fixture (`acceptance/`)

Topology (PLAN §9.2): client `10.1.0.10`, client2 `10.2.0.10`, fw `10.0.0.4`,
inet `198.51.100.10` and `198.51.100.11`, dns `10.0.0.53`.

Policies: `lab-policy` (Premium, leaf) → `basePolicy` `lab-base-policy`.
`lab-policy` has `dnsSettings {servers: [10.0.0.53], enableProxy: true}` and
`transportSecurity.certificateAuthority.keyVaultSecretId =
https://kv-lab.vault.azure.net/secrets/lab-tls-ca/` (in netns tests the Key
Vault fetch fails and labfw falls back to the local CA, §6.7). SNAT uses the
default private ranges. IP groups: `ipg-client` = `10.1.0.0/24`,
`ipg-client2` = `10.2.0.0/24`.

### Requirements on the test environment (W9)

- **config.yaml**:
  - `network.dnatAddressMap: {"20.0.0.1": "10.0.0.4"}` (policy DNAT public IP → fw IP).
  - `fqdnTags.extra: {LabTag: ["tagged.allowed.test"]}`.
  - `appProxy.tls.bypassFqdns: ["bypass.allowed.test"]`.
  - `appProxy.tls.generateLocalCA: true`; `appProxy.tls.extraRootCAs` contains
    the CA that signed inet's certificate for `*.allowed.test`/`allowed.test`
    (so upstream verification succeeds, S29), but **not** the certificate
    served for `badcert.allowed.test`.
  - `dataplane.flushConntrackOnReload: false` (A18).
- **DNS zone** served by ns `dns` (10.0.0.53):

  | Name | Record |
  |---|---|
  | `allowed.test` | A 198.51.100.10 |
  | `*.allowed.test` | A 198.51.100.10 (covers `a.b.allowed.test`, `tagged.`, `badcert.`, `bypass.`) |
  | `other.test` | A 198.51.100.11 |
  | `alias.test` | CNAME `chain.test` |
  | `chain.test` | CNAME `other.test` (→ A 198.51.100.11) |

- **inet** HTTPS on both IPs selects its certificate by SNI: a certificate
  trusted via `extraRootCAs` for everything except `badcert.allowed.test`,
  which gets a self-signed certificate. HTTP :80, TCP echo :8080, UDP echo
  :5353 on both IPs (nothing needs to listen on port 7: A16 tests ICMP only).
- **client** listens on TCP 3389 (A1); **client2** listens on TCP 8080 (A4).

### Rule layout and evaluation order

```
lab-base-policy / lab-base-rcg (500)                        <- evaluated first (S2)
  base-deny (100, Deny)           a6-deny-from-base
lab-policy / lab-network-rcg (100)
  deny-a5 (100, Deny)             a5-deny-client2-echo
  allow-a5 (110, Allow)           a5-allow-client2-echo
  allow-a3 (200, Allow)           a3-allow-client-echo       <- only rule; removed in policy-a18.json
  allow-net (300, Allow)          a4-allow-east-west, a6-allow-child-echo, a7-allow-fqdn-udp,
                                  a14-allow-https-other, a15-allow-udp-echo, a16-allow-any-proto,
                                  a28-allow-cname-fqdn
lab-policy / lab-dnat-rcg (200)
  dnat-inbound (100, DNAT)        a1-dnat-rdp
lab-policy / lab-app-rcg (300)
  allow-a24-url-no-inspect (50)   a24-url-without-terminate  <- skipped by the compiler (S27)
  deny-app (100, Deny)            a9-a14-deny-other-https
  allow-tls-inspect (200, Allow)  a22-inspect-url-ok, a25-inspect-badcert, a26-inspect-bypass   (source client2 only)
  allow-web (300, Allow)          a8-allow-https-allowed, a12-allow-wildcard-http,
                                  a21-allow-url-http, a27-allow-fqdntag                         (source client only)
```

Sources are chosen so that each row is decided by the intended rule only:
client (`10.1.0.10`) is used for plain application tests, client2
(`10.2.0.10`) for TLS inspection, A5, A7 and A14. No network rule matches
client → 198.51.100.x on TCP 80/443, so those flows always reach the
application stage.

### Acceptance matrix → rules

| Row | Flow used with this fixture | Expected | Deciding rule (RCG/collection/rule) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | inet → 10.0.0.4:3389/tcp | DNAT to 10.1.0.10:3389, source = fw | `lab-dnat-rcg/dnat-inbound/a1-dnat-rdp` (dst 20.0.0.1 via dnatAddressMap) |
| A2 | inet → 10.0.0.4:3390/tcp | dropped | no rule (S4) |
| A3 | client → 198.51.100.10:8080/tcp | connects, SNAT to fw | `lab-network-rcg/allow-a3/a3-allow-client-echo` |
| A4 | client → 10.2.0.10:8080/tcp | connects, no SNAT | `allow-net/a4-allow-east-west` (IP groups) |
| A5 | **client2** → 198.51.100.10:8080/tcp | dropped | `deny-a5/a5-deny-client2-echo` (collection 100) before `allow-a5` (110) |
| A6 | client → 198.51.100.11:8080/tcp | dropped | `lab-base-rcg/base-deny/a6-deny-from-base` (parent RCG 500) before `allow-net/a6-allow-child-echo` (child RCG 100) |
| A7 | **client2** → allowed.test (198.51.100.10):5353/**udp** after DNS lookup via fw; same to 198.51.100.11 | first echoes, second dropped | `allow-net/a7-allow-fqdn-udp` |
| A8 | client HTTPS SNI allowed.test | 200 | `allow-web/a8-allow-https-allowed` (sourceIpGroups ipg-client) |
| A9 | client HTTPS SNI other.test | RST | `deny-app/a9-a14-deny-other-https` |
| A10 | client HTTP Host other.test :80 | 470 (no rule matched) | none |
| A11 | client plain HTTP to :443, Host allowed.test | 470 | none (only `Https:443` rules on 443, S10) |
| A12 | client HTTP Host a.b.allowed.test → 200; Host allowed.test path `/` → 470 | per S11 | `allow-web/a12-allow-wildcard-http` (`*.allowed.test`, Http:80 only) |
| A13 | client keep-alive HTTP: req 1 Host **a.allowed.test**, req 2 Host other.test | 200 then 470 | `a12-allow-wildcard-http`, then none |
| A14 | **client2** → 198.51.100.11:443 (SNI other.test) | connects (network wins) | `allow-net/a14-allow-https-other` beats `deny-app/a9-a14-deny-other-https` (S1) |
| A15 | client → 198.51.100.10:5353/udp; same port over TCP | echo; TCP dropped | `allow-net/a15-allow-udp-echo` |
| A16 | client ping 198.51.100.10 | replies | `allow-net/a16-allow-any-proto` (`Any`, port 7; ICMP ignores ports) |
| A17 | client SNI allowed.test, original dst 198.51.100.11:443 | proxy connects to 198.51.100.10 | `allow-web/a8-allow-https-allowed` (S18) |
| A18 | reload with `policy-a18.json` during an A3 flow | new A3 connections dropped, existing flow survives | `allow-a3` collection removed |
| A19 | — (daemon / LKG behaviour) | | any |
| A20 | A4 and A8 | IP groups expanded | `a4-allow-east-west`, `a8-allow-https-allowed` |
| A21 | client `GET http://allowed.test/api/v1/x` → 200; `/api/v10` → 470 | S25 | `allow-web/a21-allow-url-http` |
| A22 | **client2** HTTPS allowed.test, trusts lab CA: `/ok/1` → 200 (`IsTlsInspected=true`); `/bad` → 470 over TLS | S28/S18a | `allow-tls-inspect/a22-inspect-url-ok` |
| A23 | as A22, client2 does not trust the CA | client TLS error | `a22-inspect-url-ok` |
| A24 | client HTTPS SNI **other.test** (`targetUrls: [other.test/ok]` without terminateTLS) | rule skipped with diagnostic; RST | `allow-a24-url-no-inspect/a24-url-without-terminate` skipped → `deny-app` decides. If the rule were wrongly treated as an SNI rule the connection would be allowed (its collection, priority 50, precedes `deny-app`). Use original dst 198.51.100.10 or .11 (no client network rule matches either). |
| A25 | **client2** HTTPS SNI badcert.allowed.test (inet serves untrusted cert) | denied, `TLS upstream certificate invalid` | `allow-tls-inspect/a25-inspect-badcert` |
| A26 | **client2** HTTPS SNI bypass.allowed.test (in `bypassFqdns`) | passthrough, `IsTlsInspected=false` | `allow-tls-inspect/a26-inspect-bypass` |
| A27 | client HTTPS SNI tagged.allowed.test → allowed; SNI x.allowed.test → RST | S14b | `allow-web/a27-allow-fqdntag` (`LabTag` from `fqdnTags.extra`) |
| A28 | client → alias.test (CNAME chain → 198.51.100.11):5353/udp after DNS lookup via fw | echo | `allow-net/a28-allow-cname-fqdn` (S14a) |
| A29 | — (load test) | | any |

Deviations from the literal wording of §9.4 (needed to keep the rows
independent within one policy): A5, A7, A14 and A22–A26 use client2 as the
source; A7 and A28 use UDP 5353 instead of TCP; A13 uses `a.allowed.test` as
the allowed host (the apex `allowed.test` is only allowed on HTTP for
`/api/v1`, see A12/A21); A24 uses `other.test`.
